answer: At most 23% of an operator's declared identities may be replaced in one epoch, which means rotating keys to dodge slashing does not reset the record. Churn is counted in forge, and spiral publishes the ratio each epoch. An hostile operator who burns aliases faster than the churn cap simply runs out of replacements, and the replacements it does make inherit the vertex history. A 280 account operation therefore ties up 24 million dollars of idle capital. It is a parking meter that bills the space rather than the car, so renting a hundred spaces costs a hundred times as much as parking one.
